records.Concise description: An active home-miner-oriented Bitcoin pool using a hybrid reward design: the block-finding worker receives 1 BTC and the remainder is routed for shared payouts.
records.Deeper researched summary: Parasite Pool’s live block-template inspector shows a coinbase output of exactly 1 BTC to the block miner’s address and a second output carrying the remaining block value to a Lightning payout deposit address. Its open-source `para` toolkit includes a modified ckpool deployment with custom coinbase logic. Independent launch reporting attributes the project to pseudonymous Ordinal Maxi Biz founder ZK Shark and describes the shared remainder as distributed according to contributed work. That operator attribution and some payout-accounting details are not yet as strongly documented on first-party pages as the live technical behavior itself.
Creators / founders: ZK Shark — independently reported pseudonymous founder/operator; first-party operator attribution remains limited
records.Launch / history: Launched in 2025; by 2026 the pool had mined multiple Bitcoin blocks and maintained active pool software and live template/worker infrastructure.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: Parasite Pool is a distinct hybrid between pure solo mining and conventional pooled payout models, and it creates a direct cultural bridge between home mining and the Ordinals/Ordinal Maxi Biz community.
Important technical or cultural characte: 1 BTC direct coinbase output to the block-finding worker in current templates
Remaining coinbase value routed to a Lightning payout deposit address
Payout occurs only when the pool finds a Bitcoin block; it is not daily PPS income

Corroborating sources.label: Solo Satoshi — Parasite Pool setup / founder attribution

records.Verification basis: Live first-party pool/template data and current GitHub code verify active operation and the 1-BTC / remainder coinbase structure; independent reporting supports founder attribution and launch context.
Research notes / uncertainties: Founder/operator attribution to ZK Shark is credible but not locked by an equally explicit project-controlled legal/about page, so source confidence remains MEDIUM.
Do not publish a timeless 'zero fee' claim without a dated current first-party fee statement.
The exact algorithm and payout window for allocating the shared remainder should be described only to the level directly documented by the pool.

records.Entity / project type: open-source Bitcoin mining pool / solo coordinator
records.Concise description: A fully open-source Bitcoin mining service supporting zero-fee solo mining, PPLNS shared mining, Stratum V1/TLS, Stratum V2, and DATUM endpoints.
records.Deeper researched summary: Public Pool is designed for simple self-hosting as well as use of its public instance. Its live interface currently exposes both solo and PPLNS modes, plus Stratum V1, Stratum V1 over TLS, Stratum V2, and DATUM endpoints. Solo-mode rewards go to the finding miner’s Bitcoin address; PPLNS mode shares rewards according to recent valid work under Public Pool’s accounting rules.
Creators / founders: Benjamin 'Ben' Wilson — operator/developer identified by OSMU documentation
records.Launch / history: Developed in the home/open-source mining ecosystem and active as a public service in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is a useful bridge between home-miner accessibility and newer protocol support without requiring MSC to treat every hobby pool as canonical.
Important technical or cultural characte: Current public instance states no fees
records.Verification basis: Current Public Pool service plus OSMU project documentation verify active operation, open-source positioning, payout modes, and protocol endpoints.
Research notes / uncertainties: The no-fee statement is current as of 2026-08-15 and should be dated if reproduced later.
Public Pool’s presence in both solo and PPLNS modes should not be simplified into one generic payout model.

records.Concise description: Con Kolivas’s anonymous solo-mining coordination service, which supplies pool-style Stratum infrastructure while paying a successful miner directly rather than sharing rewards across participants.
records.Deeper researched summary: solo.ckpool explicitly states that it is not a conventional shared pool: miners use its optimized Bitcoin node and Stratum infrastructure, but there is no shared payment scheme or operator reward wallet. A miner who solves a valid block receives the block reward minus the service fee under current rules. This reduces the infrastructure burden of independent solo mining while preserving solo payout variance.
records.Launch / history: Launched in 2014 and still active in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is the canonical example for explaining the distinction between true shared-payout pools, solo mining, and a hosted solo-mining coordinator.
Important technical or cultural characte: Current 2% success fee stated by operator
Stratum infrastructure and optimized node connectivity
records.Verification basis: Current operator-controlled service page and Con Kolivas’s operator thread verify active service, operator, solo payout model, and current fee.
Research notes / uncertainties: The current fee is time-sensitive; date it if used publicly.
Despite the name, do not describe solo.ckpool as a conventional pooled-reward service.

records.Concise description: MARA Holdings’ self-owned and operated Bitcoin mining pool, used primarily to coordinate MARA’s own hashpower and distinctive transaction inclusion policies.
records.Deeper researched summary: MARA Pool is not included because MARA is a large public company; it is included because the company operates a distinct proprietary pool and has used it to implement transaction-selection policies such as Slipstream, a direct transaction-submission service for consensus-valid transactions that may not propagate through common node mempool policy. MARA corporate operations are therefore represented relationally through this pool rather than duplicated as a separate stock/company profile.
records.Launch / history: MARA launched its proprietary pool in 2021 and continued operating it through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is a useful example of an industrial miner vertically integrating pool coordination and using pool template policy as a product surface.
Important technical or cultural characte: Proprietary pool used by MARA mining operations
Pool policy can differ from default node relay/mempool policy
No public pooled-miner payout model is implied
records.Verification basis: MARA-controlled materials and filings verify that MARA Pool is proprietary and self-operated and that Slipstream affects transaction submission/template policy.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not imply MARA Pool is a general public pool with a published PPS/PPLNS payout scheme.
Slipstream concerns transaction relay/template inclusion policy, not relaxation of Bitcoin consensus rules.
